purpose: Real-world abundance proxies for the locality-abundance review (proposals/REVIEW-LOCALITY-ABUNDANCE-2026-10-21.md): what each scenario's locality actually yields, as counts of photographs and of market listings, compared by tools/locality-abundance-compare.mjs against the simulator's multi-seed crystal inventory (tools/assemblage-census.mjs).

mineralienatlas.what: Photographs per mineral per locality, Mineralienatlas (Geolitho Stiftung), page LokationMineralBilder with recurse=1 (sub-localities included), summed over the listed location ids and over sub-localities.
mineralienatlas.captured_with: a real browser session (the site serves a JavaScript check to scripted clients; the review did not bypass it)
mineralienatlas.verification: sha256 of the per-locality "Name=count;" strings (sorted locality keys, "key\npairs\n" concatenated) computed in the page and on disk both = b56cf6387e184017e21d37a933f3bfbaa04be05191c2ec68c3ffc4aca7cd5604
mineralienatlas.caveat: Photo counts measure collector attention, not tonnage: rare species and type-locality species are over-photographed (the Uravan district's photos are almost all rare vanadates, not carnotite), and common gangue is under-photographed.

ebay.what: Active listing titles on ebay.com in category 3213 (Rocks, Fossils & Minerals), up to 6 pages of 240 per query, deduplicated by item id across a locality's queries; titles classified by tools/market-title-dictionary.mjs. Provenance: JSON.stringify(MARKET_TITLE_DICTIONARY) — the 363 entries — hashes to 5d3556449edfb5f27d55d9f4d880f6e56c504084f15d80d08fa85ad03a61fd35 both in the page and from the file; the lapidary pattern was injected from the file's JSON; cleanTitle and titleFamily were re-typed identically in the page (not hash-checked). The file itself hashes differently because it also holds those functions and comments.
ebay.counting: mention_families: a "family" is a title with digits, units and punctuation removed, so one seller relisting the same lot counts once; each family counts once for every species its title names. lead_families: the first species a title names. Lapidary families (cabochons, jewelry, slabs, spheres, carvings, tumbled) are excluded from both. "x:" keys are species the simulator has no engine for.
ebay.verification: sha256 of the compact summary JSON computed in the page and on disk both = cbb9cb8beeb9c2814cbd5c8c4278b2a265ba25d707bbf1946ae2725ec4bdf497
ebay.caveat: Sold-listing history needs an eBay login and was not used; active supply is a stock, not a flow. ebay.com under-represents European localities (Schneeberg, Wittichen, Grimsel), where Mineralienatlas carries the weight.

literature.what: Published abundance statements per locality, gathered by three research passes and keyed to simulator species. class: AB abundant, CO common, UN uncommon, RA rare, VR very rare, ND not documented in the sources read (ND? = absence from a few sources only), Q questionable, doc = documented without an abundance word; suffixes -crust / -coating / -oxidized qualify the form.
literature.status: V = the source was opened and the wording seen (by the research pass, or "read first-hand" by the review itself where the source note says so); S = search snippet or low-reliability page; R = recalled. Only V and S are used as evidence in the review.
literature.spot_checks: Read first-hand by the review on 2026-10-21 — 20 statements in 7 sources, all matched the research passes: Smith 1979 USGS PP 1043 p. 59 (Table 14 values; "Trona and halite are the major mineral components"; "Hanksite is the third most abundant mineral, borax the forth"); Smith & Haines 1964 USGS Bull. 1181-P (p. P1 Upper Salt composition; p. P7 celestite sentence); Lindgren & Ransome 1904 USGS Bull. 254 pp. 20-21 (calaverite/sylvanite; native gold absent except by oxidation; gangue quartz, fluorite, dolomite; celestite never in large amount; secondary K-feldspar; 1 oz Ag to 10 oz Au); Peacock 1928 Am. Mineral. 13 p. 243 (Cape Belt crocidolite exclusively); Leach et al. 2010 USGS SIR 2010-5070-A (dominant MVT minerals, barite minor to absent, fluorite rare; Zn/(Zn+Pb) < 0.1 SE Missouri; Viburnum chalcopyrite; barite never reported SE Missouri; calcite common Central Tennessee); Harvard Tsumeb Mineral Notes TSNB311 (scorodite Very rare) and TSNB324 (smithsonite Very common, Pinch & Wilson 1977 quote); Koenigsberger 1919 (Aar-granite cleft types 1, 1-prime, 1-double-prime; diorite type 5). Review round 1 independently confirmed eight more: Teale 1979; García-Ruiz et al. 2007; Bastin 1914; Weeks & Thompson 1954; Sukheswala et al. 1974; Heaney & Fisher 2003; Eggleton et al. 2011; Proust & Fontaine 2007.
literature.mindat_note: Mindat was not used as a data source (its pages are behind a Cloudflare human check). A few literature classes rest on search-snippet text from mindat; they carry status S.
